headline: High-risk workspace overlap: Cline can write and execute in the shared workspace while python-cheatsheet is documentation-only, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cline reads and writes workspace files and uses MCP/browser tools, so malicious content in shared files could influence its tool use. python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and cannot actively inject, but if Cline consumes its rendered content or copied text as instructions, the pathway exists. The shared filesystem bridge makes this plausible.
conditions: IF Cline ingests workspace text as instructions without provenance checks
IF a shared file or copied snippet contains attacker-controlled directives
mitigations: Separate the workspace directories
Disable automatic instruction-following from file contents
Require provenance tags for any imported text
Review MCP inputs before tool execution

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cline can read the filesystem and has broad network egress, so sensitive workspace content could be exposed if it is present. python-cheatsheet touches no data classes and has no file or network access, so it is not a direct leak source; the risk is Cline exfiltrating shared workspace data. The shared filesystem is the relevant bridge.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in the shared workspace
IF Cline is allowed to transmit file contents to external services
mitigations: Move secrets out of the shared workspace
Restrict Cline network egress
Use a separate non-sensitive workspace
Redact sensitive files before running Cline

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cline has write and git-modifying capabilities, but python-cheatsheet has no write, shell, or network capabilities, so there is no meaningful bidirectional conflict. The only overlap is read-only documentation access, which does not create a write race. This is a low-risk asymmetry rather than a contested mutable resource.
conditions: IF python-cheatsheet is replaced with a writable agent
IF both agents are given write access to the same git repository
mitigations: Keep python-cheatsheet read-only
Do not grant shared write access
Use separate git worktrees
Add lockfiles for any future writable pairing

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cline can generate code or browser-derived facts that a downstream agent might treat as authoritative, while python-cheatsheet is a reference-only agent that may present content without verification. If Cline's output is copied into python-cheatsheet-driven documentation or guidance, errors can cascade into incorrect actions or code. The pair lacks an explicit verification step.
conditions: IF Cline outputs unverified facts that are reused downstream
IF python-cheatsheet content is treated as authoritative guidance without checking
mitigations: Add a human verification step
Require source links for any factual claims
Mark generated content as untrusted
Use a checklist before publishing downstream outputs

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, with no PHI, residency, or retention commitments stated. Cline handles model-provider API keys and browser screenshots, but python-cheatsheet touches no regulated data classes, so there is no documented compliance mismatch. The absence of compliance metadata limits the finding to a low-confidence, low-severity gap.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into Cline's workspace
IF an external policy requires residency or retention guarantees not documented here
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in the workspace
Document retention settings
Review API-key handling
Add a data-class policy before deployment
